content.user_title: Evaluate UX Components with Structured Reviews
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent UX feedback before changing interface components. This skill applies a three-part framework for position, visual weight, and spacing.
actual_capabilities: Reviews buttons, navigation, forms, and utility controls against documented UX criteria.
Compares component placement with common product conventions.
Assesses visual hierarchy between primary, secondary, and utility actions.
Checks spacing, touch target size, and visual grouping guidance.
Produces prioritized recommendations with rationale and UX references.
limitations: Does not replace usability testing with real users.
Focuses on UX structure, not full visual branding.
Requires enough UI context, such as screenshots, code, or descriptions.
Reference coverage is strongest for buttons and common navigation.

use_cases.title: Review a Button Group
use_cases.description: Check action order, prominence, labels, spacing, and touch target size before implementation.

use_cases.title: Resolve Design Feedback
use_cases.description: Turn subjective comments about layout or hierarchy into clear recommendations with supporting principles.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Audit
use_cases.description: Identify priority UX issues in key screens before a product launch or stakeholder review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Component Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI component for position, visual weight, and spacing. Explain what is correct and what should change.

prompt_templates.title: Navigation Evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a header or navigation area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this navigation header against common product conventions. Include placement, hierarchy, spacing, and prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Flow Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison between two layout options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two layout options for a signup flow. Assess primary actions, secondary actions, touch targets, and accidental click risks.

prompt_templates.title: Release UX Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-release review of a full screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interactive screen before release. Use the three-dimension framework, cite relevant UX principles, and rank fixes by user impact.

output_examples.input: A header places Sign Up, Sign In, and a theme toggle together on the left.
output_examples.output: The review flags action order and utility placement. It recommends placing Sign In before Sign Up, with the theme toggle separated on the far right.

output_examples.input: A form has two filled buttons labeled Continue and Cancel with a four pixel gap.
output_examples.output: The review identifies competing visual weight, vague action text, and tight spacing. It recommends a ghost secondary button and clearer action labels.

output_examples.input: A mobile checkout screen has a small primary button below several secondary links.
output_examples.output: The review prioritizes touch target size and hierarchy. It recommends a larger primary action and lower visual weight for secondary links.

best_practices: Provide screenshots, component code, or precise layout descriptions for accurate evaluation.
Ask for separate findings by position, visual weight, and spacing.
Request priorities when deciding which UX changes to implement first.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a full brand redesign when you need a component UX review.
Do not rely on the skill without user testing for critical flows.
Do not provide vague descriptions when spacing or placement matters.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates UI position, visual weight, spacing, labels, and common interaction conventions.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it review screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes, when the host assistant can inspect images or when the user describes the screen clearly.

faq.question: Is it only for buttons?
faq.answer: No. It also covers navigation, forms, utility controls, spacing, and hierarchy.

faq.question: Does it generate final UI code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on evaluation and recommendations, though an assistant may implement changes separately.

faq.question: How should I get the best result?
faq.answer: Share the component context, user goal, screen state, and any design guideline you want considered.
